node.title: Exact locator-prefix consumer and null-fiber scope
node.statement: Let D be a finite evaluation domain, A=K+t, and Phi_{A,t}(S) the first t sub-leading coefficients of the monic locator of an A-subset S. For every prefix z, the polynomial word U_z=X^A+sum_{i=1}^t z_i X^{A-i} has an exact bijection between Phi_{A,t}^{-1}(z) and its Reed-Solomon codewords of degree <K agreeing on A points. Consequently a universal exact-list upper ledger must control the heaviest relevant prefix fiber after its paid strips, not only the zero or t-null fiber. In characteristic p, t-nullity fixes only the p-free prefix coordinates; p-multiple locator coefficients are free. Moreover raw mode-at-null is false: for D=F_17^*, A=9, t=1, the zero fiber has size 672 and every nonzero fiber has size 673. Therefore any null-fiber route requires a separately proved strip-aware max-to-null or exchange-compression theorem.
